source_text:
Homilia in assumptionem Christi
Τοῦ ἐν ἁγίοις Πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἐπιφανίου ἐπισκόπου Κύπρου εἰς τὴν
ἀνάληψιν τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεός.
Κόσμος σώματος ἡ ἐπιτεθεῖσα τῷ σώματι κεφαλή· κόσμος δὲ τῶν ἑορτῶν ἡ
σήμερον ἑορτή. Τί γάρ; φησί. Χριστοῦ ἀνάληψιν μετὰ σαρκὸς ἑορτάζομεν, ὡς τῶν
∆εσποτικῶν ἑορτῶν δεικνυμένην πλήρωμα. Καθάπερ γὰρ κεφαλὴ φαιδρόμορφος,
οὕτω καὶ ἡ σήμερον ἑορτὴ τῆς θεϊκῆς χάριτος ἀπαυγάζει τὸ κάλλος· ἀλλ' οἱ πολλοὶ
ἀγνοοῦντες τὸ ταύτης μέγεθος, ἧττον αὐτὴν νομίζουσι. Καὶ εἰ βούλεσθε μαθεῖν,
ἀνεξικάκως συντείνατέ μοι τὸν νοῦν. Μόνον μοι δι' εὐχῶν συνεργήσατε, παρακαλῶ·
καὶ τὰς μολιβδώδεις αὔρας καταστείλατε· καὶ τὰ κύματα τῆς φλυαρίας γαληνιάσατε·
καὶ σχολάζουσάν μοι τὴν ἀκοὴν παράσχητε. Κατὰ γὰρ τὸν σοφὸν Σολομῶντα, λόγοι
σοφῶν ἐν ἀναπαύσει ἀκούονται.
Πρώτη τοίνυν 43.480 ἑορτὴ ἡ φρικτὴ καὶ θαυμαστὴ κατὰ σάρκα τοῦ Χριστοῦ
γέννησις. Πῶς γὰρ οὐ θαυμαστὴ ἡ ἐξ οὐρανῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ πρὸς ἡμᾶς κατάβασις,
μᾶλλον δὲ συγκατάβασις; ὅτι ὁ πάντων ∆εσπότης τὴν τοῦ δούλου μορφὴν ἑνῶσαι
ἑαυτῷ κατηξίωσε, καὶ πτωχὴν μητέρα ἔχειν ὁ πάντα περιέχων. ∆ευτέρα ἑορτὴ ἡ τῶν
Θεοφανίων πολλῷ τῆς πρώτης τὴν θεωρίαν μείζω ἔχουσα. Ἐν μὲν γὰρ τῇ πρώτῃ
ἑορτῇ ὑπεδείκνυε τὸν τεχθέντα Θεὸν Λόγον ἀστήρ· ἐν δὲ τῇ δευτέρᾳ ἑορτῇ Ἰωάννης
ἐβόα, Ἴδε ὁ Ἀμνὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁαἴρων τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ κόσμου. Ἐβεβαίου δὲ τὴν
μαρτυρίαν τοῦ βαπτιζομένου οὐρανόθεν βοῶν ὁ Πατήρ· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Υἱός μου ὁ
ἀγαπητὸς, ἐν ᾧ ηὐδόκησα. Ἀλλ' οὐδὲ τότε ὁλόκληρος ἡ τῆς σωφροσύνης ἀπόλαυσις,
ἐπειδὴ μηδέπω τὸ θνητὸν σῶμα διὰ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τὴν ἀθανασίαν ἐδέξατο. Τρίτη
ἑορτὴ τοῦ σωτηριώδους πάθους ἡ ἀνάστασις ζωοποιεῖ τοὺς διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος τοῦ
αἵματος αὐτοῦ μαρμαρυγὰς ἀπαστράπτοντας, καὶ ἀναγεννωμένους δι' ὕδατος καὶ
Πνεύματος ἁγίου. ∆ιὸ καὶ πεσόντα κόσμον ἀνέστησε, καὶ τὸν πάλαι ἐκπεσόντα Ἀδὰμ
ζωῆς αἰωνίου ἠξίωσε.
∆ιὰ ξύλου ὁ Ἀδὰμ θάνατον ἐτρύγησε· διὰ ξύλου σταυροῦ ζωὴν τῷ κόσμῳ
χαρίζεται. Καὶ αὕτη μὲν τῶν προλαβουσῶν ἑορτῶν ἐνδοξοτέρα ἀνεδείκνυτο, ἐπειδὴ
ἐν αὐτῇ ὁ θάνατος διὰ θανάτου τὸν θάνατον θανατώσας, καὶ ζωὴν ἀθάνατον τοῖς
θανοῦσιν ἐπήγαγεν. Ἀλλὰ καὶ αὐτὴ οὐκ εἶχε τῆς χαρᾶς τὴν πληρότητα ἐπὶ γῆς τὸν
ἀναστάντα κατέχουσα. Καὶ ἡ τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς δὲ χαρὰν μεγάλην καὶ ὑπὲρ λόγον, ἐν
ᾗ τοῖς ἀποστόλοις ἐδίδοτο Πνεῦμα ἅγιον· σήμερον δὲ ἐν τῇ τῆς Ἀναλήψεως ἡμέρᾳ
πάντα διὰ πάντων εὐφροσύνης πεπλήρωται. Οὐρανοὺς τοὺς φεγγοτόκους ἀνοίξας,
καὶ τὸν λεπτομερέστατον ἀέρα βαθμώσας, καὶ τὸν ἐκ γῆς εἰς τὰς οὐρανίους ἁψίδας
ἀνασφαιρώσας, καὶ πάσας τὰς τῶν ἀγγέλων φύσεις εἰς χαρὰν ἄληκτον παρορμήσας,
ξένην ἡμῖν θέαν ἐπέδειξε, τὴν ἡμετέραν σάρκα ἐπὶ θρόνου βασιλικοῦ ἐπηρμένην.
Ποῦ εἰσὶν οἱ περὶ τὰ ἱπποδρόμια ἀσχολούμενοι, καὶ ἡνιόχων ἀγαπῶντες ὀξύτητα;
∆εῦτε, ἴδετε παράδοξον ἱπποδρόμιον· τὸν τῆς κτίσεως ∆ημιουργὸν ἐν ἀνθρωπίνῳ
thought_title: The Ascension as crown of the feasts
orientation: Epiphanius opens his homily by ranking the feasts of Christ and arguing that today's feast of the Ascension surpasses them all.
pass_a_gloss: Homily on the ascension of Christ. Of our father among the saints Epiphanius bishop of Cyprus on the ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ. Blessed is God. An ornament of the body is the head placed upon the body; and an ornament of the feasts is today's feast. For what? he says. We celebrate the ascension of Christ with flesh, as the fullness of the dominical feasts being shown. For just as a head beautiful in form, so also today's feast radiates the beauty of divine grace; but the many, not knowing its greatness, consider it lesser. And if you wish to learn, patiently direct your mind to me. Only help me through prayers, I ask; and calm the leaden breezes; and still the waves of idle talk; and grant me a hearing at leisure. For according to the wise Solomon, words of the wise are heard in quiet. First then is the feast, the awesome and wondrous birth of Christ according to the flesh. For how is not wondrous the descent of God from heaven to us, or rather the coming down? because the Master of all deemed worthy to unite to himself the form of a servant, and the one who contains all things to have a poor mother. Second feast is the feast of Epiphany, having a contemplation much greater than the first. For in the first feast a star pointed out the born God the Word; but in the second feast John cried out, Behold the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world. And the Father confirmed the testimony of the one being baptized, crying from heaven: This is my Son, the beloved, in whom I was well pleased. But not even then was the enjoyment of self-control complete, since not yet did the mortal body receive immortality through the resurrection. Third feast is the resurrection of the saving passion; it gives life to those flashing forth radiances through the baptism of his blood, and being born again through water and holy Spirit. Therefore it raised up the fallen world, and deemed worthy of eternal life Adam who fell long ago. Through a tree Adam harvested death; through the tree of the cross he grants life to the world. And this one was shown more glorious than the preceding feasts, since in it death, having put death to death through death, brought immortal life to the dead. But this one too did not have the fullness of joy, holding on earth the one who rose. And the feast of Pentecost had great joy beyond speech, in which the holy Spirit was given to the apostles; but today on the day of the Ascension all things through all things have been filled with gladness. Having opened the light-bearing heavens, and having made the finest air into steps, and having raised up from earth to the heavenly vaults, and having urged all the natures of angels to unending joy, he displayed to us a strange sight, our flesh lifted up on a royal throne. Where are those busy around the hippodromes, and loving the swiftness of charioteers? Come, see a paradoxical hippodrome: the Creator of creation in a human

choices.why: Glossary term for God's condescension in becoming human; the author corrects κατάβασις to the stronger συγκατάβασις.
Glossary term for the feast of Christ's baptism when the Trinity was manifested.
Glossary term; here it refers to the full enjoyment of salvation not yet complete before the resurrection.
The verb suggests lifting up as into a sphere or vault; rendered plainly to keep the literal force of upward motion.

choices.english: having made the finest air into steps
choices.why: Literal rendering of the image of Christ making the air into a staircase for his ascent.
The author uses the chariot-race venue as a metaphor for Christ's ascent; kept as a loanword to preserve the image.

bible_refs.note: Ἴδε ὁ Ἀμνὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ αἴρων τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ κόσμου
Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητὸς, ἐν ᾧ ηὐδόκησα
λόγοι σοφῶν ἐν ἀναπαύσει ἀκούονται; attributed to Solomon

pass_b_english: A homily of our father among the saints, Epiphanius, bishop of Cyprus, on the ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ.

A head placed upon a body is the body's crowning glory, and today's feast is the crowning glory of all the feasts. Why? Because we celebrate the ascension of Christ with his flesh, shown to be the completion of all the feasts of the Lord. For just as a head is radiant in form, so today's feast shines out with the beauty of divine grace. Yet many people do not recognize its greatness, and they think less of it. If you want to learn, then patiently give me your attention. Only help me with your prayers, I beg you: calm the leaden breezes, still the waves of idle talk, and lend me ears that are free from distraction. For as the wise Solomon says, the words of the wise are heard in quiet (Ecclesiastes 9:17 LXX).

The first feast, then, is the awesome and wondrous birth of Christ according to the flesh. For how is it not wondrous, the coming down of God from heaven to us—or rather, his coming down in condescension? Because the Master of all things deigned to unite to himself the form of a servant, and he who contains all things deigned to have a poor mother. The second feast is Epiphany, which offers a far greater vision than the first. For at the first feast a star pointed to the birth of God the Word; but at the second feast John cried out, "Look, the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world" (John 1:29). And the Father confirmed the testimony concerning the one being baptized, crying out from heaven, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (Matthew 3:17). But even then the enjoyment of self-control was not yet complete, because the mortal body had not yet received immortality through the resurrection. The third feast is the resurrection from the saving passion, which gives life to those who through baptism flash with rays of his blood and are born again through water and the Holy Spirit. Therefore it raised up the fallen world and counted the ancient fallen Adam worthy of eternal life.

Through a tree Adam harvested death; through the tree of the cross Christ grants life to the world. And this feast was shown to be more glorious than the feasts that came before, because in it death, having put death to death through death, brought immortal life to the dead. But even this feast did not possess the fullness of joy, since it held the risen one on earth. And the feast of Pentecost also held great joy, beyond words, in which the Holy Spirit was given to the apostles. But today, on the day of the Ascension, all things in every way have been filled with gladness. He opened the light-bearing heavens, made the finest air into steps, raised the one from earth to the heavenly vaults, and stirred all the natures of the angels to unending joy. He showed us a strange sight: our own flesh lifted up upon a royal throne.
Where are those who busy themselves with hippodromes and love the speed of charioteers? Come, see a paradoxical hippodrome: the Creator of creation in human

problems.source_quote: Κατὰ γὰρ τὸν σοφὸν Σολομῶντα, λόγοι σοφῶν ἐν ἀναπαύσει ἀκούονται
problems.why: The quote 'words of the wise are heard in quiet' matches Ecclesiastes 9:17 LXX, not Proverbs 1:5.

problems.quote: the enjoyment of self-control was not complete
problems.source_quote: Ἀλλ' οὐδὲ τότε ὁλόκληρος ἡ τῆς σωφροσύνης ἀπόλαυσις
problems.why: Glossary defines σωφροσύνη as 'self-control' in sense of chastity/yoke bearing thirtyfold fruit; here context demands 'chastity' or the ascetic sense, but more critically the phrase refers to the incomplete state before resurrection, not 'self-control' as modern virtue. However, checking: the glossary bans 'moderation, temperance' and gives 'self-control' as English. The real issue: ἀπόλαυσις means 'completion, fulfillment' not 'enjoyment'—the joy/fulfillment was not complete.
problems.fix: the fulfillment of joy was not yet complete

problems.quote: made the finest air into steps
problems.why: βαθμόω means to make into steps/degrees, but 'finest air' for λεπτομερέστατον ἀέρα is odd; more critically, the image is of Christ ascending through the air making it into steps/degrees for his ascent, not 'made the finest air into steps' which is unclear. However, main issue: 'raised up from earth' lacks object—'him' or 'the one from earth' is missing, making sentence ungrammatical and unclear who is raised.
problems.fix: and raised the one from earth to the heavenly vaults
problems.ruling: 'ἀνασφαιρώσας' means 'raising/rolling away'; English 'raised up from earth' lacks object, breaking syntax and meaning.

edits.old: the enjoyment of self-control was not complete
edits.new: the fulfillment of joy was not yet complete

edits.old: raised up from earth to the heavenly vaults
edits.new: raised the one from earth to the heavenly vaults

fixed: Proverbs 1:5 LXX → Ecclesiastes 9:17 LXX: the quote 'words of the wise are heard in quiet' matches Ecclesiastes 9:17 LXX, not Proverbs 1:5.

the enjoyment of self-control was not complete → the fulfillment of joy was not yet complete: ἀπόλαυσις means fulfillment/completion, not enjoyment; the sentence refers to the incomplete state of joy before the resurrection.
raised up from earth to the heavenly vaults → raised the one from earth to the heavenly vaults: the Greek has an object (τὸν ἐκ γῆς), so 'the one from earth' is needed for grammatical clarity.

problems.quote: the fulfillment of joy was not yet complete
problems.source_quote: οὐδὲ τότε ὁλόκληρος ἡ τῆς σωφροσύνης ἀπόλαυσις
problems.why: σωφροσύνη means self-control/chastity, not 'joy'; wrong sense entirely
problems.fix: the enjoyment of self-control was not yet complete

problems.quote: flash with radiance through the baptism of his blood
problems.why: μαρμαρυγάς are flashes/rays they flash, not 'baptism of his blood'
problems.fix: who flash with rays of his blood

edits.old: the fulfillment of joy was not yet complete
edits.new: the enjoyment of self-control was not yet complete

edits.old: flash with radiance through the baptism of his blood
edits.new: flash with rays of his blood

fixed: σωφροσύνη means self-control, not joy; corrected to 'the enjoyment of self-control was not yet complete'.
μαρμαρυγάς means flashes/rays, not baptism; corrected to 'flash with rays of his blood'.

problems.quote: to those who flash with rays of his blood
problems.source_quote: τοὺς διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος τοῦ αἵματος αὐτοῦ μαρμαρυγὰς ἀπαστράπτοντας
problems.why: Omits 'through baptism' (διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος), dropping the sacramental link between baptism and the radiance of Christ's blood.
problems.fix: to those who through baptism flash with rays of his blood
problems.ruling: Source διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος τοῦ αἵματος links radiance to baptism; English drops βαπτίσματος, losing that tie.

problems.quote: confirmed the testimony of the one being baptized
problems.source_quote: Ἐβεβαίου δὲ τὴν μαρτυρίαν τοῦ βαπτιζομένου
problems.why: The objective genitive refers to John's testimony about Christ; 'of the one being baptized' implies Christ gave the testimony.
problems.fix: confirmed the testimony concerning the one being baptized
problems.ruling: μαρτυρίαν τοῦ βαπτιζομένου is witness about Christ; English 'of' misleads as Christ's testimony.

edits.old: to those who flash with rays of his blood
edits.new: to those who through baptism flash with rays of his blood

edits.old: confirmed the testimony of the one being baptized
edits.new: confirmed the testimony concerning the one being baptized

fixed: omission baptism: edited — source has διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος τοῦ αἵματος αὐτοῦ, English omitted through baptism
agency testimony: edited to concerning — source Ἰωάννης ἐβόα ... Ἐβεβαίου ... ὁ Πατήρ shows τοῦ βαπτιζομένου is John's testimony about Christ
Ecclesiastes citation: no edit — source λόγοι σοφῶν ἐν ἀναπαύσει ἀκούονται is Ecclesiastes 9:17 LXX, not Proverbs 1:5
enjoyment to fulfillment: no edit to current enjoyment of self-control — correct for τῆς σωφροσύνης ἀπόλαυσις per glossary self-control
raised the one: no edit — correct for τὸν ἐκ γῆς εἰς τὰς οὐρανίους ἁψίδας ἀνασφαιρώσας
fulfillment to enjoyment: no edit — current enjoyment of self-control already correct for τῆς σωφροσύνης ἀπόλαυσις
rays without baptism: edited — same as omission; restored through baptism for διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος

last_rejected.why: Glossary bans 'condescension'; required term is 'coming down'.
last_rejected.ruling: συγκατάβασις means 'coming down with/condescension'; both senses valid; no glossary shown.

last_rejected.why: Context is about resurrection completing joy, not 'self-control'; σωφροσύνη here means salvation/integrity of the body.
last_rejected.ruling: σωφροσύνη normally means self-control/modesty; 'enjoyment of self-control' is within range.

last_rejected.quote: those who flash with rays of his blood
last_rejected.why: Misread syntax: αἵματος goes with βαπτίσματος (baptism of blood/martyrdom), not 'rays of his blood'.
last_rejected.fix: those who flash with the rays of baptism, even of blood
last_rejected.ruling: Greek τοῦ αἵματος αὐτοῦ μαρμαρυγὰς ἀπαστράπτοντας naturally reads 'flashing rays of his blood'.

last_rejected.quote: made the finest air into steps
last_rejected.why: βαθμόω means 'made into steps/degrees', but 'finest air' misrepresents λεπτομερέστατον (subtle/rarefied).
last_rejected.fix: made the most subtle air into steps
last_rejected.ruling: λεπτομερέστατον = 'finest/most subtle'; 'finest air' is acceptable rendering.

last_rejected.source_quote: τὸν ἐκ γῆς εἰς τὰς οὐρανίους ἁψίδας ἀνασφαιρώσας
last_rejected.why: ἀνασφαιρόω means 'caused to ascend in a sphere/orbit', not simply 'raised'; 'the one' obscures Christ as subject.
last_rejected.fix: caused him from earth to ascend in a sphere to the heavenly vaults
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνασφαιρόω means 'raise/launch upward'; 'raised' is adequate; 'the one' = Christ contextually.

last_rejected.source_quote: κατὰ τὸν σοφὸν Σολομῶντα, λόγοι σοφῶν ἐν ἀναπαύσει ἀκούονται
last_rejected.why: The quote matches Ecclesiastes 9:17 in some versions, but the LXX reference is uncertain; the Greek matches Sirach 9:17 or similar wisdom texts more closely.
last_rejected.fix: Sirach 9:17 or Wisdom of Solomon (verify citation)
last_rejected.ruling: Quote matches Ecclesiastes 9:17 LXX exactly; Sirach 9:17 differs; reference is correct.
